## TL;DR

The Agents page's Build Your Team, Scheduled Tasks and Reminders sections now have
long-list coverage at 375, 768 and 1280 px. Each case runs against fixtures, in
headless WebKit, with the real components mounted in jsdom. The pass found one real
layout bug: a long unbroken schedule name ran past its card at 375 and 768 px. I fixed
it in `ScheduledTasksPanel.vue` and added an assertion that would have caught it. The
QA record is `docs/qa/2026-11-agents-long-lists-qa.md`. The 27 cases in the browser
test file pass after the fix, and the post-fix screenshot shows the title wrapping
inside its card.

## Work and rationale

The task asked for 50+ entries with long names, checked at three widths, and form
validation in plain English. The repo already had `agents-page-qa-browser.test.ts`
from an earlier pass (#1223). That pass stubbed `ScheduledTasksPanel`,
`RemindersPanel` and `BuiltInAgentCard` with `true`, so none of those panels had been
rendered with real data. I extended the same file rather than starting a second
harness. Its WebKit helpers (`openFixturePage`, `audit`, `expectFits`) are already
tested, and a second copy would have drifted.

I added three long-list cases that mount the real panels against Pinia stores, with
`fetch` stubbed. Each case asserts the item count, so a broken render can't pass
silently: 60 schedules, 60 reminders and 55 custom agents. Titles mix 96-character
unbroken strings with long sentences, and reminder links carry a long model label.
Two form cases trigger the real validation: an invalid schedule timezone and a
cleared reminder date. Each asserts the plain-English message and then checks at
three widths that the open editor still fits.

The first run found no overflow in the viewport audit, but my first look at the
375 px screenshot showed a title running past its card edge. The audit checks element
boxes against the viewport, so text that stays on screen but leaves its card was
never flagged. The schedule title's flex container lacked `min-width: 0`, and the
title had no `overflow-wrap`, so the unbroken name ran past the border. I fixed the
CSS and added `expectInsideCards`, which compares each inner text element against
its card's border.

To confirm the new assertion catches the regression, I removed the
`overflow-wrap` rule and ran the test. It failed at 375 and 768 px with 12 overflowing
names per width. I restored the rule, and the test passes. I then re-rendered the
375 px screenshot and checked it: the 96-character name wraps across four lines and
the toggle stays in place.

## Approaches tried

I first considered a separate QA test file. Duplicating about 120 lines of harness
would have meant two copies to keep in step, so I went with extending the existing
file. I also considered stubbing the whole `AgentsView` for the Build Your Team
case, as the earlier pass did. Instead I mounted it with 55 custom agents, because
the stubbed version would not have exercised the long custom-agent list. That case
keeps `BuiltInAgentCard` stubbed, which is a real gap I document rather than hide.

For the layout check I tried `scopedCss` on `AgentsView` and `AgentCard`. Neither
file has a `<style>` block, so the scoped-CSS path was wrong. The global stylesheet
already covers them, and the case passes empty CSS, like the existing agent-list case.

## Challenges and blockers

Vitest's default config does not load the Vue plugin, so the first run failed to
parse `.vue` files. The UI config (`src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`, via `bun run test:vitest`)
fixes that. `head -n -1` is not supported on macOS, so I spliced the file with `sed '$d'`.

The scheduled-task and reminder rows hold text that is only visible inside cards, and
the viewport audit can't see text that overflows its card. That is why the new card
assertion exists, and why I checked the screenshot instead of trusting the first
green run.

## Key learnings

A viewport-edge audit is not enough for long text. Text can stay on screen and still
run past its card's border. Check inner text against its container, not only the
viewport. Confirm a new assertion fails on the unfixed code before trusting it.

Stubbing a whole child panel with `true` hides exactly the layout that long lists
break. For a QA pass, mount the real component with fixture data and assert the item
count, so a broken render can't pass.

Screenshots still catch what geometry assertions miss. The unbroken-title bug was
only obvious when I looked at the rendered image.

Limits: persistence against the real backend was not exercised, the built-in team
cards are stubbed, and no human has checked these screens on a device.
